anatomy.flutter: ContextMenu(child, children, width, enabled) is a StatefulWidget wrapping a Popover with anchor: Listener(onPointerDown) + SelectionContainer.disabled(child), and content: MenuContent(children, width, minWidth: Menu.minWidthMenu, onClose).
anatomy.web: ContextMenu > ContextMenuTrigger (select-none div) and ContextMenuPortal > ContextMenuContent, with ContextMenuItem/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Label/Separator/Sub/SubTrigger/SubContent as the same slot list documented in menu.dart, reused across dropdown-menu and menubar.

api.flutter: ContextMenu's fields are child, children: List<MenuChild>, width, enabled — MenuChild is the shared sealed class (MenuItem, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuRadioItem/Group, MenuLabel, MenuSeparator, MenuSub) from menu.dart, and ContextMenu.sideOffset is fixed at space(0.5) = 2.
api.web: ContextMenuContent takes collisionPadding (default 8) plus every Radix ContextMenuPrimitive.Content prop; ContextMenuItem takes variant: "default"|"destructive" and inset; ContextMenuCheckboxItem/RadioItem take checked/value — matching MenuItemVariant, MenuCheckboxItem and MenuRadioItem/Group one-for-one.
api.note: side="right", align="start" and sideOffset=2 are hardcoded constants on both sides (ContextMenu.sideOffset in context_menu.dart line 69, and Radix's own context-menu default that context-menu.tsx never overrides), so there is no prop drift between the two APIs beyond collisionPadding vs no configurable padding constant in Dart, which is cosmetic since MenuContent still clamps to the viewport.

states.flutter: _ContextMenuState toggles _at (the pointer's global Offset) between null and a value on a kSecondaryButton PointerDownEvent, driving Popover(open: _at != null) — rest is _at == null, open is _at != null with the popover's own hover/pressed row states inside MenuContent.
states.web: The docs States block lists rest ("no visual change of its own"), open ("Radix positions it at the pointer and sets data-state=\"open\""), disabled item ("announced but inert, skipped by arrow-key navigation") and destructive (red text, placed last below a separator) as the full matrix, with loading/success/error/empty marked N/A.

disabled.flutter: MenuItem, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuRadioItem and MenuSub all carry a disabledReason: String? field (menu.dart lines 199, 239, 262, 355) that is "shown as a tooltip while [enabled] is false" — the disabled row explains itself.
disabled.web: CLOSED: ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuCheckboxItem and ContextMenuRadioItem now take disabledReason?: string (components/ui/context-menu.tsx). When given, the item is wrapped in components/ui/disabled.tsx's Disabled (mode="aria", since Radix's menu Item is a role="menuitem"/"menuitemcheckbox"/"menuitemradio" div with no native disabled attribute to carry) — an always-on aria-describedby merges the reason onto the row for a screen reader regardless of whether the popover is ever opened, and a small info affordance beside the row makes it click/tap-reachable without disturbing arrow-key navigation. ORIGINAL: ContextMenuItem/CheckboxItem/RadioItem only forward Radix's disabled prop through data-disabled:pointer-events-none data-disabled:opacity-50 (context-menu.tsx lines 103, 162, 192) — there is no tooltip, title, or any text explaining why an item is disabled anywhere in the file or its doc page.
disabled.note: CLOSED 2026-09-11: measured in the dev server (http://localhost:3111, desktop-dark) — opening the context menu and tabbing/arrowing to a disabled item with disabledReason set reads the reason via its aria-describedby association; the info button opens a Popover on click/Enter/Space. Pinned by a new unit test (test/context-menu.test.tsx) and by e2e/gaps-disabled.spec.ts (keyboard reachability + announcement). ORIGINAL: Flutter's disabledReason tooltip has no web counterpart: a disabled ContextMenuItem on the web just dims and stops responding to clicks, with nothing telling the reader why it is unavailable, unlike the Dart widget's explicit self-explaining affordance.

interaction.flutter: _ContextMenuState only listens for onPointerDown with buttons & kSecondaryButton set (a mouse/trackpad secondary press) — the file's own doc comment states the port "has no long-press or keyboard route" of its own.
interaction.web: Radix's ContextMenuTrigger (node_modules/@radix-ui/react-context-menu dist/index.mjs) wires onContextMenu (which the browser also dispatches for Shift+F10/the Menu key) AND a 700ms longPressTimerRef for touch, per handleOpen and the setTimeout at line 104 — richer than the Dart trigger.
interaction.note: This is the browser doing work Flutter's widget layer has no equivalent for: the DOM contextmenu event is natively reachable by keyboard (Shift+F10/Menu key) and Radix adds its own touch long-press timer, so the web offers two extra entry points the Flutter port never attempts to replicate — correctly, since those are platform affordances rather than component logic.

semantics.flutter: Popover positions MenuContent with anchorPoint at the raw pointer Offset and origin: PopoverAnchorMode.corner, matching side: PopoverSide.right/align: PopoverAlign.start — the measured web offsets (dx=2, dy=-0.44) that ContextMenu.sideOffset codifies as space(0.5).
semantics.web: Docs Accessibility block: "Content role: menu. Items are role=\"menuitem\", role=\"menuitemcheckbox\" or role=\"menuitemradio\"" and "Disabled items: Announced but not actionable, and skipped by arrow-key navigation" — standard ARIA menu roles from Radix, unremarked-on but present in context-menu.tsx via the primitive.
